rationale:
PINS rule R7 for scala at the only two places the analyzer can publish a placeholder literal: a TYPE POSITION and an EXPRESSION READ. The construct is the LANGUAGE's wildcard. `Class[?]` (Scala 3) and `Class[_]` (Scala 2) parse as generic_type > type_arguments > type_identifier, so the type-name walk reached the wildcard and published it as a referenced TYPE; `$_` / `${_}` in an interpolated pattern parse as interpolation > identifier("_"), so the expression walk published `_` as a read. Measured over the WHOLE corpus through production parseFile (18,965 files, script/m14/tmp/scala4-census.mts): 876 unresolvable placeholder endpoints in files with ZERO parse diagnostics — 867 `references` (874 spelled `?`, 2 `_`, 2 `*`), 8 `uses` (all `_`), 1 `instantiates` (`_`). Named sources: compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/config/Properties.scala:24, library/src/scala/collection/ArrayOps.scala:1037 and 1236, compiler/src/dotty/tools/backend/sjs/JSCodeGen.scala:1239 and 1457, repl/src/dotty/tools/repl/AbstractFileClassLoader.scala:86-92, project/scripts/bisect.scala:261, tests/pending/run/t7715.scala:21. This is the same defect class SCALA3 closed for `exports` (an `export p.{x => _, _}` publishing `*`), reached by a route nobody had walked.

THE POSITIVE HALF IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF, and it is why the fix is POSITIONAL rather than a literal ban. `def *` and `def ?` are legal Scala method names — library/src/scala/Char.scala declares six `*` overloads, and 17 `?` targets plus 191 `*` targets on the corpus resolve to a real declaration. `unknown` is a legal `val` name (library/test/scala/collection/IterableTest.scala:89 declares `val unknown: IterableFactory[LinearSeq]`). A rule that refused `?`, `*` or `unknown` in every position would delete 210+ real edges while removing the 876 fabrications, and would look like a win on the count. So: the type walk refuses `?` and `_`, which cannot be a TYPE name in any position; the expression walk refuses `_`, which cannot be an IDENTIFIER in any position; `*`, `?` as a member read and `unknown` are pinned here as present so the forbids cannot be widened to them.

Every wildcard spelling the corpus uses is pinned: `Class[?]`, `Class[_]`, a wildcard among other arguments (`java.util.Map[?, String]`), and two wildcards nested (`List[Map[?, _]]`). The positive rows pin that the CONCRETE types beside a wildcard survive — dropping the whole argument list instead of the wildcard would pass every forbid and lose the edge.
